title: Given the root of a binary tree, determine whether it is height-balanced, meaning that for every node the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by at most one.
shortTitle: Balanced Binary Tree: check height diff ≤ 1 at every node
keyPoints: A balanced tree has left and right subtree heights differing by at most one at every node
The efficient approach fuses height computation with the balance check in a single post-order pass
A sentinel value of -1 signals imbalance and short-circuits the rest of the computation
The naive approach recomputes heights at every node, degrading to O(n * h) which is quadratic on skewed trees
The sentinel-based short-circuit keeps the fused approach linear: once imbalance is found, no more work is done
The top-level answer is simply whether the helper avoided returning the sentinel

s1_definition.oneliner: At every node the left and right subtree heights must differ by at most one, checked in a single post-order pass that short-circuits on the first violation.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Height-balanced** – for every node, `|leftHeight - rightHeight| <= 1`.
- **Efficient approach** – a single post-order recursion returns each subtree's height, or -1 (sentinel) the moment any imbalance is found.
- **Short-circuit** – once -1 is returned, it propagates immediately without further computation.
- **Naive approach** – computes height separately at every node; O(n * h) time, quadratic on skewed trees.
- **Complexity** – efficient approach is O(n) time, O(h) space.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of the National Bank of India's reporting tree and a rule that no manager's two sides should be lopsided: one branch of reports cannot be much deeper than the other. Each manager compares how deep their left team goes versus their right team. If any manager's two sides differ by more than one level, the whole structure is declared unbalanced.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Fused Height + Balance Check

       ACC-100
      /       \
   ACC-050   ACC-150
   /
  ACC-025
  /
 ACC-010

  Post-order visits:
  ACC-010: left=0, right=0, diff=0, return 1
  ACC-025: left=1, right=0, diff=1, return 2
  ACC-050: left=2, right=0, diff=2 > 1 → return -1 (UNBALANCED)
  ACC-100: left=-1 → short-circuit, return -1

  Result: -1 → not balanced
```

```text
  Sentinel Short-Circuit Flow

  checkHeight(ACC-100)
    ├─ checkHeight(ACC-050)
    │    ├─ checkHeight(ACC-025)
    │    │    ├─ checkHeight(ACC-010) → 1
    │    │    └─ checkHeight(null) → 0
    │    │    diff = 1, ok → return 2
    │    └─ checkHeight(null) → 0
    │    diff = 2 > 1 → return -1  ← imbalance detected!
    └─ left == -1 → return -1     ← short-circuit, skip right subtree
  Final: -1 → false
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A binary tree is height-balanced when at every node the heights of its left and right subtrees differ by at most one. The naive approach computes heights separately at each node, which recomputes over and over and degrades to quadratic time on skewed trees. The efficient approach fuses height computation with the balance check in a single post-order pass.

The helper returns the subtree's height, or a sentinel of -1 the moment any imbalance is found. The sentinel propagates immediately: the parent checks for -1 before recursing further, so no unnecessary work is done after the first violation. This short-circuit is what keeps the algorithm linear.

The technique of fusing a property check with a value computation in a single recursive pass appears throughout tree problems: diameter, maximum path sum, and balance check all share this pattern.

In our banking system at National Bank of India, the account-number index is a binary search tree whose lookup speed depends on balance. After a batch of inserts, the health check uses this fused approach to confirm the index is still balanced. If it is not, the service schedules a rebalance job because a lopsided index drives lookups toward linear time, which is unacceptable for a high-traffic account service.

Remember one sentence: fuse height computation with a balance check in post-order, return -1 as a sentinel to short-circuit the moment any node is unbalanced.
